Consult Summary:
Middle-aged male with 5-day history of cough, coryza, sore throat, low-grade dyspnea and subjective fevers; likely viral URTI/early influenza. Background of type 2 diabetes and hypertension; delayed amoxicillin script issued with supportive care advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Probable viral upper respiratory tract infection / early influenza.
  • Onset Saturday (≈5 days ago); symptoms: predominantly dry cough (minimal sputum), runny nose, sore throat, mild ear dullness, diffuse myalgias/stiffness, one episode of diarrhea (resolved), subjective fever with night sweats, mild shortness of breath without chest pain.  
  • No documented wheeze, chest pain, or hemoptysis; appetite preserved, drinking fluids.  
  • Examination/vitals not performed (telephone consult).  
  • Differential: evolving lower respiratory tract infection; bacterial super-infection.  
  • Management: rest, hydration, regular paracetamol for fever, delayed script for amoxicillin (one tablet three times daily) to commence if no improvement in 24–48 h; review if not better by next week.

Issue 2:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  • On oral metformin; control parameters not discussed.

Issue 3:
- Hypertension.
  • On lisinopril; latest BP not provided.

Medications:
- Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Aspirin (occasional, OTC) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Amoxicillin (delayed prescription) – one tablet three times daily; strength not documented.  
- Paracetamol (advised PRN for fever) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
- Hypertension.  
- Overweight/obesity noted by patient.

Social History:
- Lives with wife; children moved out.  
- Factory worker (steel parts manufacturing).  
- Alcohol: ~9 pints beer/week.  
- Smoking: occasional cigarette use; transitioning to vaporizer to reduce.  

Preventative History:
- No information on screenings or vaccinations documented.

Physical Examination:
- Telephone consultation; no vitals or physical findings recorded.

Plan:
- Rest, adequate oral fluids, and nutrition.  
- Paracetamol for pyrexia/aches as needed.  
- Delayed start amoxicillin if no improvement or worsening in 24–48 h.  
- Return for face-to-face assessment or sooner if: worsening breathlessness, chest pain, persistent fever, inability to maintain oral intake.  
- Routine follow-up next week if symptoms persist.  
- Encourage smoking cessation and moderation of alcohol intake.  
- Continue regular diabetes and hypertension medications; consider review of chronic disease control at next visit.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing clinically expected elements: objective vitals, examination findings, medication doses, vaccination/screening status, recent diabetes/BP control data.  
● No internal transcript conflicts detected.  
● Transcript quality: clear but conversational; no inaudible segments.
